# Trip write API — schema reference

Everything an agent needs to write a trip without discovering the schema by
trial: the routes, the exact body of each one, the block-kind rules, and
payloads that are validated by this file's own generator. It is **generated
from the code**, so it cannot describe a schema that has moved on.

Companion pieces:

- `backend/scripts/api_write.py` — the client, and the only thing that should
  write trip content from an agent (it validates a plan before the first call,
  normalizes what the server would 422 on, and resolves venues in the right
  order). `--help` is the CLI recipe.
- The content-agent skill (`kiseki-trip-content`) — the *how-to* for a trip
  build: roadbook → days → blocks → photos → polish.

## Authentication and shape of a call

- Credentials ride in the `Authorization` header; the client reads the
  access token from `KISEKI_TOKEN`.
- Every write answers with the **canonical trip document** — reread it rather
  than assuming what landed.
- IDs are UUIDs; dates are ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`; money is a number plus a
  separate `currency`.
- `extra=forbid` is the norm: an unknown field is a 422, not a warning.

## Block-kind rules

The write model for a block is deliberately coarse — one flat `BlockFields` for
every kind — and the *kind* rules are enforced on top of it in
`app/write.py::_validate_block_kind_fields`. It keys on **presence**
(`model_fields_set`), not truthiness, which is the trap:

| Field(s) | Valid kind(s) | Error when given to another kind |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `distance`, `duration`, `route`, `via`, `from`, `to`, `mode` | `transport` | `Field(s) [...] are only valid on transport blocks` |
| `html` | `custom` | `Field 'html' is only valid on custom blocks` |
| `items` | `todo`, `gallery` | `Field 'items' is only valid on todo/gallery blocks` |

`"items": []` is therefore *not* a harmless empty array — it is a 422 that stops
a 43-block pass at block 1. So is `"distance": null` on a meal. Both arrive on
their own the moment a plan is built by round-tripping a `GET`, because a GET
returns every key with its default filled in.

`api_write.py fill` removes both client-side before the first call
(`normalize_plan`), and rejects only the class that is a genuine authoring
mistake — a *non-empty* value for another kind's field.


### `DayCreate` vs `DayPatch` — a new day takes two calls

`POST /days` takes `date`, `index`, `title` **only**. `notes`, `map` and `meta` are `DayPatch` fields, so a day the
plan creates gets them in a second call, once it has an id —
`api_write.py fill` does that itself (`day_create_extras`) and prints it in
`--dry-run`. Splitting a plan by hand was a whole throwaway script in #255.

## Venue resolution

A venue key (`placeId`) is what turns a block's Maps pill from a city search
into the actual place. `api_write.py fill` resolves them at the end of the
run, and `resolve-places <trip_id>` re-runs just that pass:

1. A registry location without a `placeId` is resolved **by name**, biased
   toward the trip's own coordinates (`GET /api/places/search?q=&lat=&lng=&radius=`).
   The bias matters: "Hotel Presidente" is a Madrid hotel as well as a San
   José one, and an unbiased search can place a venue on another continent
   without anything in the response saying so. A hit still far from the trip
   is reported in `locations_off_trip`, never written quietly.
2. A **venue block** (`activity`, `lodging`, `meal`, `booking`) copies the
   `placeId` of the registry entry its `location` points at. There is
   deliberately no free-text venue field on a block (#220) — free text is
   what let a venue look resolved while its `placeId` stayed empty.

So: put the venue in the `locations` registry, then point the block's
`location` at that entry's name. `blocks_without_venue` in the run summary
is the list of blocks that still name no venue.

## Examples

### A `fill` plan

A plan is a partial trip document: every key is optional, every write is a
merge, and absent means *leave it alone*. Top-level keys are exactly
`crew`, `days`, `features`, `locations`, `practical`, `scalars`, `sections`.
A `day` that matches an existing date is updated in place; a new one is
created (and then patched with its `notes`/`map`/`meta`, which `POST /days`
does not accept — see below). A `block` is matched on
(container, kind, title), which is what makes a re-run update instead of
stacking a second copy of the itinerary.

```json
{
  "scalars": {
    "title": "Example: three days in Kyushu",
    "stage": "planned"
  },
  "locations": [
    {
      "name": "Fukuoka",
      "kind": "city"
    },
    {
      "name": "Ohori Park",
      "kind": "venue"
    }
  ],
  "days": [
    {
      "date": "2027-04-02",
      "title": "Arrival",
      "notes": "Nothing booked yet — decide on the hill.",
      "blocks": [
        {
          "kind": "transport",
          "time": "09:40",
          "title": "AMS → FUK",
          "from": "Amsterdam",
          "to": "Fukuoka",
          "mode": "flight",
          "distance": 9200,
          "duration": "13h05"
        },
        {
          "kind": "lodging",
          "title": "Hotel Okura Fukuoka",
          "location": "Fukuoka",
          "placeId": "ChIJ_example_place_id",
          "bookingCode": "OK-4417",
          "cost": 210,
          "currency": "EUR"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "date": "2027-04-03",
      "title": "City day",
      "blocks": [
        {
          "kind": "activity",
          "time": "10:00",
          "title": "Ohori Park",
          "location": "Ohori Park",
          "description": "Loop the pond, then coffee."
        },
        {
          "kind": "meal",
          "time": "13:00",
          "title": "Yatai lunch",
          "location": "Fukuoka",
          "cost": 18,
          "currency": "EUR"
        },
        {
          "kind": "todo",
          "title": "Before we go",
          "items": [
            {
              "label": "Book the yatai tour",
              "done": false
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

```bash
api_write.py fill <trip_id> --file plan.json --dry-run   # what will be sent
api_write.py fill <trip_id> --file plan.json             # one ordered run
```

`fill` then reports what only the server can know: days without blocks,
blocks that name no venue, and locations that resolved outside the trip's
own area.

### One body per block kind

All kinds: `activity`, `booking`, `custom`, `gallery`, `link`, `lodging`, `meal`, `note`, `todo`, `transport`.
Statuses a block may carry:
`booked`, `done`, `planned`.

**transport**

```json
{"kind": "transport", "time": "08:15", "title": "Drive to Reno", "from": "Sacramento", "to": "Reno", "mode": "car", "distance": 220, "duration": "2h20", "via": "I-80"}
```

**lodging**

```json
{"kind": "lodging", "title": "Hotel Presidente", "location": "Hotel Presidente", "placeId": "ChIJ_example_hotel", "bookingCode": "PR-2210"}
```

**meal**

```json
{"kind": "meal", "time": "20:00", "title": "Dinner at the camp", "location": "Black Rock City", "cost": 0, "currency": "USD"}
```

**activity**

```json
{"kind": "activity", "time": "11:00", "title": "Bike the playa", "location": "Black Rock City", "links": [{"label": "Map", "url": "https://example.org/map"}]}
```

**todo**

```json
{"kind": "todo", "title": "Packing", "items": [{"label": "Goggles", "done": false}, {"label": "Bike lock", "done": true}]}
```

**gallery**

```json
{"kind": "gallery", "title": "Day one", "items": ["2026-08-30-1402.jpg", "2026-08-30-1500.jpg"]}
```

**note**

```json
{"kind": "note", "title": "Water", "description": "Playa water is alkali."}
```

**booking**

```json
{"kind": "booking", "title": "Camp pass", "location": "Black Rock City", "bookingCode": "BRC-9931"}
```

**custom**

```json
{"kind": "custom", "title": "Shade plan", "html": "<p>Two tarps, one pole.</p>"}
```

**transport**

```json
{"kind": "transport", "title": "Flight home", "mode": "flight"}
```


## Common 422s, and what they mean

| Error | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Field(s) ['mode', 'to'] are only valid on transport blocks` | transport-only field on another kind — including an explicit `null`/`[]` from a GET round-trip | `normalize_plan` drops it in `fill`; drop it from the plan otherwise |
| `Field 'items' is only valid on todo/gallery blocks` | `"items": []` on any other kind | same — presence is the trigger, not truthiness |
| `Extra inputs are not permitted` | unknown field on an `extra=forbid` body | check the body table above; the field does not exist |
| `Field 'html' is only valid on custom blocks` | `html` on a non-`custom` block | use `description`, or make the block `custom` |
| `cost must be a NUMBER` | `"€40"` instead of `40` + `currency` | number in `cost`, ISO code in `currency` |
| `days[N] repeats date ...` | the same date twice in one plan | `POST /days` does not dedupe by date — it creates a second day |
| `Field(s) ['notes'] are not permitted` on `POST /days` | `DayCreate` is `extra=forbid` | let `fill` do it (see above) — the `notes` go in a follow-up `PUT /days/<id>` |

## Keeping this honest

`backend/tests/test_write_api_docs.py` re-renders the file and fails if it
differs from what is committed, so a model or route change without a
regenerated doc breaks the build instead of the next agent's run.
